title: What If All the Ice on Earth Melted?

scenes.text: What if every piece of ice on Earth melted? The sea would rise about seventy metres.
Antarctica alone holds enough for fifty-eight of those metres. Greenland adds seven more.
Seventy metres is a twenty-storey building. Mumbai, Shanghai, New York and London would be underwater.
Florida would be gone. So would Bangladesh, the Netherlands and most of Denmark.
The good news: it would take thousands of years, even at today's warming.
The bad news: we are already melting it. Seas have risen about twenty-five centimetres since nineteen hundred.

description:
What if all the ice on Earth melted?
About 70 metres of sea-level rise: 58 from Antarctica, 7 from Greenland. Coastal megacities go under. It would take millennia — but it has started.
